$comment: Committed contract for WordPress core's option-write pipeline: update_option(), add_option(), and the sanitize_option() they both call. Consumers: tests/WpCoreContractTest.php (both its always-on stub-fidelity job and its oracle-dependent staleness job) and tests/tools/generate-wp-core-option-contract.php (the regeneration CLI). This exists because four of ten prior tasks each shipped a green test suite over a stub behaviour that was untrue about real core. Building this contract surfaced two further divergences (a fifth and sixth bug, in the same lineage): sanitize_option_{$option} dispatched with 2 args instead of core's 3, and the generic update_option/updated_option/add_option actions not firing at all. Both were fixed in tests/bootstrap.php on review (see 'known_gaps' below, now empty) rather than left as recorded exceptions -- the whole premise of this contract is that a documented gap and a landmine are the same object at different distances.

source.oracle: staging (ssh -p SSH_PORT root@staging-host.example, docker exec -u 33 staging-wp sh -lc 'cat /var/www/html/wp-includes/{option,formatting}.php') -- the version actually running production/staging, preferred per this task's instructions
source.cross_checked_against: local checkout /home/cody/arl-local (WordPress 6.8.7) -- tests/tools/wp-core-option-contract-extractor.php's output is byte-for-byte identical (PHP `===` on the decoded arrays) between the two for every function this contract covers; wp-includes/option.php lines 847-1190 are line-for-line identical between the two checkouts as plain text
source.extracted_with: tests/tools/generate-wp-core-option-contract.php <wp-includes-dir> <wp-version>, then hand-merged into this file's source_truth key

scope: Only the hook dispatches lexically inside WordPress core's update_option()/add_option() (wp-includes/option.php) and sanitize_option() (wp-includes/formatting.php) -- the option lifecycle only, per this task's brief. The default_option_{$option} filter both option.php functions also call is deliberately excluded from the hook list (it is an existence/default-value check used to pick a code path, not a change-notification hook), but its presence is still asserted by the extractor's raw-dispatch-count check, so its removal or duplication is not silently invisible either. esc_url()/wp_kses()-class behavioural bugs are explicitly out of reach of this structural approach and are not attempted here.

source_truth.$comment: Mechanically regenerable via tests/tools/generate-wp-core-option-contract.php -- see that file's docblock for exact invocation and the two-step (regenerate, then hand-review sequences/known_gaps) process for updating this after a WordPress core version bump. Each entry is the hook exactly as it is dispatched in core's own source, in the order it appears in that function's body.

sequences.$comment: Hand-composed test scenarios, each a full ordered walk of every hook dispatch tests/bootstrap.php's update_option()/add_option() stub ACTUALLY produces for a given call pattern (not just the source_truth hooks in isolation) -- this is what tests/WpCoreContractTest.php's always-on job exercises and asserts against. `expected_args` is what the STUB passes, which for every entry here now equals source_truth's `args` (`stub_matches_core: true` throughout -- see 'known_gaps', now empty). `fires: false` entries assert the named hook is NEVER observed for that scenario; they still carry source_truth's true args/kind/dynamic for reference, but there is nothing to compare since nothing fires.

update_option_first_write.note: fired a second time inside the add_option() this first write delegates into -- core does the same (sanitize_option() has no memory of who called it); original_value here is whatever value the delegation passed in, not the original caller's raw input.
